future_consumers.title: Owner live-promotion review for parameter stacks

master_plan_principles_consumed.principle_text: Replay and paper lanes must use the same locked identity and later emit separate result packets; PR #91 may not collapse those lanes.
Dual-result review may compare result metrics but may not merge, overwrite, average away, collapse, reinterpret, or convert either lane result into live authority.
Dual-result review requires separate replay and paper result packets that reference the same shared input identity.
Replay/paper and review identity must match runtime resolver snapshot, input lock, replay_paper input identity, and owner policy snapshot.

Dual-result review may classify non-live state and route negative, ambiguous, partial, conflicting, stale, or source-gapped results to retest, repair, revitalization, source-evidence retrieval, owner review, or rejected archive.
Dual-result review pass routes only to owner live-promotion review required and never creates live, canary, order, runtime cash, AtomicRows mutation, blocker reduction, or profit authority.
No automatic live promotion, owner approval, limited-live canary eligibility, live reachability, order execution, runtime cash receipt, or profit evidence may be inferred from dual-result review.
AtomicRows is inventory and authority ledger, not a trader or source of live authority.
QTT must transform an edge into a role-complete parameter stack; single-parameter or single-algorithm trade selection is forbidden.
Required stack roles include SIGNAL, SCORING, NORMALIZATION, RISK, EXECUTION, CAPITAL, LATENCY, ERROR_GUARD, and the repo-required QUANTUM_ADVISORY metadata role.
Blocked rows may appear only as blocked metadata or diagnostic receipts and must not enter active selected stacks, handoff, competition, or review.
Quantum optimizers may assist ranking, combinatorial search, scenario sampling, and parameter-stack refinement, but remain outside live order submission and cannot create quantum advantage evidence.
Classical execution gates remain final for execution release, and the Execution Router remains the final order-submission authority.
Source, connector, runtime cash, order, and fill facts require accepted-source or runtime receipts where policy requires them; PR #91 creates none.

Do not invent values, IDs, source evidence, optimizer defaults, venue semantics, SDK behavior, financial constants, quantum backend values, runtime receipts, replay/paper results, review evidence, test pass claims, AtomicRows bundle creation, or zip ingestion success.
